title.en: Health factors across the life course

intro.zh-CN: 从每天的行为、生活条件和身体指标理解健康。先选择年龄阶段查看重点，再结合因素目录形成可执行的观察与行动计划。
intro.en: Understand health through daily behaviour, living conditions and body measures. Start with stage priorities, then use the factor directory to plan observations and actions.

title.en: How to read numbers and sources

text.zh-CN:
先确认数字说的是谁、什么结果和多长时间。

- 原报告的综合排名和简化GRADE式字母分级属于作者整理，本知识页按主题组织，不将它们展示为官方排名或个人评分。
- 随机治疗试验的平均相对风险、环境参考值和日常活动建议不是同一尺度，不能直接相加。
- 各节保留支持该内容的来源和适用范围。
text.en:
Check the population, outcome and timeframe before using a number.

- The source report’s composite ranking and simplified GRADE-style letters are author-created; this resource uses topics rather than presenting them as official rankings or personal scores.
- Average relative effects from treatment trials, environmental references and activity recommendations are different measures and cannot be added.
- Each section retains the sources and applicability supporting its content.

title.zh-CN: 生物学、家族史与发育背景

summary.zh-CN: 记录与生俱来和早期形成的易感性，帮助选择更合适的检查与预防时机。
summary.en: Record inherited and early-life susceptibility to guide the timing of assessment and prevention.

text.zh-CN:
家族与出生经历影响疾病机会，也影响需要哪些支持。

- 家族成员共享基因，也常共享饮食和环境；家族聚集不能全部归因于遗传。
- 早产儿的器官发育尚未完成，后续照护可能更需要关注呼吸、喂养和发育。
text.en:
Family and birth history influence risk and support needs.

- Relatives share genes as well as food and environments; clustering is not entirely genetic.
- Organs are less mature after preterm birth, so follow-up may particularly address breathing, feeding and development.

text.zh-CN:
把背景写成可核对的事实。

- 记录近亲患过什么病、何时发病，尤其多人患同类疾病或很年轻时发病。
- 儿童保留孕周、出生体重和新生儿治疗记录；不知道的资料标为未知，后续再补。
text.en:
Use a factual record that can be checked.

- Record relatives’ diagnoses and ages at onset, particularly similar illness in several relatives or unusually early disease.
- Keep gestational age, birth weight and neonatal care records for children; mark missing information as unknown.

text.zh-CN:
带背景资料参加常规就诊，让它改变可执行的安排。

- 医生可据家族史调整筛查开始时间，必要时转遗传咨询，先明确检测会回答什么问题。
- 早产或发育需要额外支持的儿童，按随访计划观察进展；发现能力落后或原有技能丢失时及时评估。
text.en:
Bring the history to routine care so it informs practical decisions.

- Family history may change when screening starts; genetic counselling can clarify what a proposed test would answer.
- For prematurity or developmental needs, follow the monitoring plan and seek assessment for delayed progress or loss of established skills.

text.zh-CN:
这些背景帮助决定关注重点和检查时机。

- 家族史同时包含环境与行为，常见病风险仍会受后来的暴露和照护影响。
- 遗传检测针对具体疾病和问题，应先明确结果会怎样影响后续检查或照护。
text.en:
This background helps guide attention and the timing of assessment.

- Family history also reflects environment and behaviour; later exposures and care still affect common-disease risk.
- Genetic testing addresses particular conditions and questions; first clarify how a result would change assessment or care.

title.zh-CN: 饮食质量与生命早期营养

summary.zh-CN: 关注吃进去的食物是否足量、多样和适龄，以及哪些摄入妨碍健康。
summary.en: Consider whether food is sufficient, varied and age-appropriate, and which intakes contribute to harm.

text.zh-CN:
食物提供生长、修复和维持身体活动的原料。

- 长期摄入不足可能妨碍生长或导致营养缺乏；只减少热量并不等于营养更好。
- 蔬菜、水果、豆类和全谷物提供纤维与多种营养；盐过多会增加血压负担。
text.en:
Food supplies the material for growth, repair and daily activity.

- Insufficient intake can impair growth or cause deficiencies; eating fewer calories is not the same as better nutrition.
- Vegetables, fruit, pulses and whole grains provide fibre and nutrients; excess salt increases blood-pressure burden.

text.zh-CN:
记录常吃什么，比只记一种所谓健康食品更有用。

- 看一周中蔬果、全谷物、豆类和蛋白质食物是否经常出现，也记录含糖饮料、加工肉与咸调味料。
- 婴幼儿记录喂养方式、辅食种类和进食困难；体重与生长变化转到“脂肪量与生长”一起看。
text.en:
Look at the usual eating pattern rather than one claimed healthy food.

- Review vegetables, fruit, whole grains, pulses and protein foods across the week, together with sugary drinks, processed meat and salty seasonings.
- For young children, record feeding method, complementary foods and feeding difficulties; assess growth using the linked growth factor.

text.zh-CN:
先调整容易持续的食物选择，并照顾特殊阶段。

- 用水替换一部分含糖饮料，增加蔬菜豆类和全谷物；成人按WHO建议将一天总盐量控制在5克以下，包含调味料和加工食物中的盐。
- WHO建议前6个月纯母乳，约6个月开始安全、营养充分的辅食并继续母乳至2岁或更久；喂养困难应获得实际支持，确保婴儿摄入足够。
- CDC建议可怀孕人群每天获得400微克叶酸，以预防部分脑和脊柱发育缺陷；既往相关缺陷或特殊用药者由产科确认方案。
text.en:
Start with sustainable food changes and life-stage needs.

- Replace some sugary drinks with water and add vegetables, pulses and whole grains. WHO advises adults to keep total salt below 5 grams daily, including salt in sauces and processed foods.
- WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months, safe nutritious complementary food from around 6 months, and continued breastfeeding to 2 years or beyond. Feeding difficulties need practical support to ensure sufficient intake.
- CDC recommends 400 micrograms of folic acid daily for people capable of pregnancy to prevent some brain and spine defects; previous affected pregnancies or relevant medicines require an obstetric plan.

text.zh-CN:
建议关注长期饮食模式和具体缺乏，不能由单一食品推算寿命。

- 儿童需求随年龄改变；孕期、肾病、吞咽困难或明显消瘦时，应调整餐食而非直接套用减重饮食。
- 喂养、补充剂与盐的建议有各自适用对象；已确诊缺铁等问题需同时查原因，相关诊疗见病症正文。
text.en:
Advice concerns long-term patterns and specific deficiencies, not lifespan estimates from a single food.

- Children’s requirements change with age. Pregnancy, kidney disease, swallowing difficulty or marked weight loss calls for adapted meals rather than a standard weight-loss diet.
- Feeding, supplement and salt recommendations have distinct audiences. Established iron deficiency also requires cause assessment; use the linked condition for clinical details.

summary.zh-CN: 血压反映血管承受的压力；重复、规范测量能发现没有感觉的长期风险。
summary.en: Blood pressure reflects force on blood vessels; repeated sound measurements reveal risk that may be silent.

text.zh-CN:
血液压力长期过高，会增加心脏和血管负担。

- 收缩压是心脏收缩时的压力，舒张压是放松时的压力；两者需一起看。
- 持续升高可损害脑、心和肾，即使当下没有头痛或不舒服。
text.en:
Persistent high pressure strains the heart and blood vessels.

- Systolic pressure is the pressure during a heartbeat; diastolic pressure is during relaxation. Both matter.
- Sustained elevation can harm the brain, heart and kidneys even without headache or discomfort.

text.zh-CN:
关注多次读数与测量条件。

- 使用合适袖带，向医护人员学习姿势和记录方法；保留日期、读数、是否不适及正在用药。
- 诊室与家庭结果可能不同；让医生判断是否需要家庭多日记录或全天监测，单次偏高与长期升高要分清。
text.en:
Record repeated readings and the conditions of measurement.

- Use a suitable cuff, learn positioning and recording from a professional, and keep dates, readings, symptoms and current treatment.
- Clinic and home readings can differ. Ask whether home records or day-and-night monitoring would clarify an isolated elevation versus persistent high pressure.

text.zh-CN:
把记录交给医疗团队，并同时处理影响血压的生活因素。

- 反复偏高时预约评估，协商复查和目标；饮食减盐、合适活动与处方治疗各有作用。
- 已有心血管病、肾病、孕期或治疗后站起头晕时，要重新核对目标和耐受；药物选择与危险行动见高血压正文。
text.en:
Review the record with the care team and address relevant daily habits.

- Arrange assessment for repeated high readings and agree follow-up and targets; salt reduction, suitable activity and prescribed treatment each contribute.
- Cardiovascular or kidney disease, pregnancy or standing dizziness during treatment calls for a target and tolerability review. See the hypertension article for medication and urgent-care detail.

text.zh-CN:
随机治疗研究支持降低血压能够减少心血管事件。

- 2021年汇总48项试验、344716人的研究中，收缩压降低5 mmHg与主要心血管事件相对风险约降低10%对应。
- 这是群体治疗效果，不等于每个人的绝对风险减少10个百分点；具体目标仍取决于病情与治疗耐受。
text.en:
Randomised treatment evidence supports fewer cardiovascular events with blood-pressure reduction.

- A 2021 analysis of 48 trials with 344716 participants found about a 10% relative reduction in major cardiovascular events per 5 mmHg lower systolic pressure.
- This population treatment effect is not a 10-percentage-point absolute benefit for each person; targets still depend on clinical context and tolerability.

summary.zh-CN: 血糖检查用于识别持续糖代谢异常，检查种类和怀孕状态会改变解释。
summary.en: Glucose tests identify persistent problems with glucose regulation; interpretation depends on the test and pregnancy.

text.zh-CN:
血糖是血液中的葡萄糖，是身体的能量来源之一。

- 当身体调节葡萄糖的能力出现问题，血糖可能持续偏高，医生需进一步分清糖尿病类型。
- 症状、家族史、体重及既往妊娠糖尿病等信息帮助决定何时检测。
text.en:
Blood glucose is sugar circulating as one source of energy.

- Impaired regulation can leave glucose persistently high; further assessment determines the type of diabetes.
- Symptoms, family history, weight and previous gestational diabetes help decide when testing is useful.

text.zh-CN:
检查反映的时间范围不同。

- 空腹血糖是一个时间点；HbA1c（糖化血红蛋白）大致反映过去3个月的平均水平。
- 贫血、血红蛋白变异及妊娠某些阶段可干扰HbA1c；与血糖结果不一致时要请医生解释。
- 保留是否空腹、检测单位和妊娠状态；家用血糖仪可以按治疗计划监测，但不能单独确诊。
text.en:
Tests describe different time windows.

- Fasting glucose is a snapshot; HbA1c, glycated haemoglobin, reflects roughly the preceding 3 months.
- Anaemia, haemoglobin variants and parts of pregnancy can distort HbA1c; ask about disagreement with glucose results.
- Record fasting status, units and pregnancy. Home meters can support an agreed monitoring plan but do not independently establish a diagnosis.

text.zh-CN:
让复查和病因判断跟上检测。

- 无明确急症时，异常结果通常需要进一步确认，之后再商定饮食、活动和治疗计划。
- 孕期一般于24–28周筛查妊娠糖尿病，存在既往糖尿病或其他风险时更早评估；孕期采用相应标准。
text.en:
Follow testing with confirmation and clinical assessment.

- Without a clear emergency, abnormal results usually need confirmation before agreeing a diet, activity and treatment plan.
- Gestational diabetes is generally screened at 24–28 weeks; existing diabetes or other risks prompt earlier assessment, using pregnancy-specific criteria.

text.zh-CN:
筛查异常、确诊与治疗目标是不同问题。

- 检测能发现问题，但仅凭结果不能区分所有糖尿病类型，也不能直接决定某一种药。
- 非孕诊断界值与孕期治疗目标不同；已确诊者的低血糖风险、用药和随访见相关病症正文。
text.en:
An abnormal screen, a diagnosis and a treatment target are different questions.

- Tests identify abnormalities but do not distinguish every diabetes type or automatically select a medicine.
- Nonpregnancy diagnostic cutoffs differ from pregnancy treatment targets; use the linked condition for hypoglycaemia, medicines and follow-up after diagnosis.

summary.zh-CN: 了解运送胆固醇的颗粒及长期风险，避免只追求一张化验单上的单个箭头。
summary.en: Understand cholesterol-carrying particles and long-term risk, rather than one flagged number.

text.zh-CN:
胆固醇是身体需要的物质，通过脂蛋白颗粒在血中运送。

- 低密度脂蛋白胆固醇（LDL-C）过高可促进血管壁脂质斑块，影响血流并增加心脑血管事件。
- 遗传和日常习惯都影响血脂；体形偏瘦或没有不适也可能存在异常。
text.en:
Cholesterol is needed by the body and travels in lipoprotein particles.

- High low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, LDL-C, can promote fatty arterial plaque, impairing flow and increasing cardiovascular risk.
- Inherited factors and daily habits both affect lipids; a lean build or lack of symptoms does not establish normal levels.

text.zh-CN:
保留完整结果及检测时的治疗情况。

- 记录总胆固醇、LDL-C、HDL-C和甘油三酯的单位与时间，不把它们当作同一个指标。
- 同时说明既往心脑血管病、家族早发病史和降脂药使用；这些信息影响结果的临床意义。
text.en:
Keep the full result and treatment context.

- Record dates and units for total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C and triglycerides; they describe different aspects of blood lipids.
- Include previous cardiovascular disease, early disease in relatives and lipid medicines, which change how results are interpreted.

text.zh-CN:
将饮食和活动与需要的医疗治疗结合。

- 减少高饱和脂肪食物，选择能够长期维持的饮食与活动；遗传性升高仍可能需要药物。
- 复查用于判断变化和治疗反应，目标结合总体风险确定；具体诊断、药物和副作用见血脂异常正文。
text.en:
Combine sustainable habits with indicated medical care.

- Reduce foods high in saturated fat and build a sustainable food and activity pattern; inherited elevation may still need medicine.
- Repeat testing assesses change and treatment response, with targets based on overall risk. See the dyslipidaemia article for diagnosis, medicines and adverse effects.

text.zh-CN:
降低LDL的随机试验提供了治疗效果证据。

- 2012年27项试验个体数据荟萃分析中，他汀使LDL-C降低1 mmol/L，主要血管事件相对风险约降低21%（RR 0.79，95%置信区间0.77–0.81）。
- 该结果来自他汀试验，并非每个人固定获益21%；原有风险和随访时间影响实际减少多少事件。
text.en:
Randomised LDL-lowering trials provide evidence of treatment benefit.

- A 2012 individual-data analysis of 27 statin trials found about 21% lower relative risk of major vascular events per 1 mmol/L reduction in LDL-C (RR 0.79, 95% confidence interval 0.77–0.81).
- This is a statin-trial result, not a fixed 21% benefit for each person; baseline risk and follow-up affect the absolute number of events prevented.

summary.zh-CN: 把成人脂肪负担与儿童生长放在年龄合适的参照中，关注长期变化。
summary.en: Interpret adult body fat and childhood growth using age-appropriate references and trends.

text.zh-CN:
身体大小既受营养影响，也受遗传、疾病和环境影响。

- 脂肪过多可能增加代谢和心血管负担；原因常涉及多种因素，不能仅用意志解释。
- 儿童正在长高长重，关注是否沿适合自己的轨迹生长，比把体重与成人标准比较更合适。
text.en:
Body size reflects nutrition, inheritance, illness and environment.

- Excess fat can add metabolic and cardiovascular burden; multiple causes matter beyond willpower.
- Children are growing in height and weight, so age-appropriate trajectories are more useful than adult weight standards.

text.zh-CN:
测量用于发现需要进一步评估的变化。

- 成人BMI是体重（kg）除以身高（m）的平方，单位为kg/m²，是便宜的初筛指标；结合腰围和身体情况理解脂肪分布。
- 儿童使用年龄和性别相应的生长图，保留连续身高和体重记录；婴幼儿喂养情况也需一起看。
text.en:
Measurements identify changes worth assessing.

- Adult BMI is weight in kilograms (kg) divided by height in metres (m) squared, expressed in kg/m², a low-cost screening measure; waist size and clinical context add information about fat distribution.
- Use age- and sex-appropriate growth charts for children and retain serial height and weight measurements alongside feeding history in young children.

text.zh-CN:
把目标设在可持续的营养与生活变化上。

- 成人可与团队讨论饮食、活动及必要治疗；儿童由家庭共同改善餐食和活动环境，避免自行套用成人节食。
- 明显无意消瘦、孩子长势停滞或进食困难时，应评估营养和疾病原因，而不是只继续减重。
text.en:
Focus on sustainable nutrition and daily-life changes.

- Adults can discuss food, activity and indicated treatment; families can improve children’s meals and activity environment without applying adult restrictive diets.
- Marked unintentional weight loss, faltering growth or feeding difficulty warrants assessment for nutritional or medical causes rather than continued weight reduction.

text.zh-CN:
同一个体重或BMI不代表相同身体组成和健康状态。

- 儿童与成人的分类方式不同；年龄、族群和其他健康状况影响风险解释。
- 将BMI与腰围结合解释，并用同一个人的连续记录观察变化。
text.en:
The same weight or BMI does not imply identical composition or health.

- Children and adults use different classification systems; age, population background and other health conditions affect interpretation.
- Interpret BMI alongside waist measurements and follow change using serial records for the same person.

summary.zh-CN: 记录产品、使用和被动暴露，优先让家庭和工作场所免受烟雾影响。
summary.en: Track products, use and passive exposure, and work toward smoke-free homes and workplaces.

text.zh-CN:
烟草会影响多个器官，尼古丁还会造成依赖。

- 吸烟与癌症、心血管和呼吸疾病有关；二手烟也伤害不吸烟的人。
- 儿童和青少年发育中的大脑更易受尼古丁影响，电子烟与加热烟草也应纳入暴露记录。
text.en:
Tobacco affects many organs, while nicotine creates dependence.

- Smoking contributes to cancer, cardiovascular and respiratory disease; second-hand smoke also harms people who do not smoke.
- Developing brains are particularly vulnerable to nicotine. Include e-cigarettes and heated tobacco in exposure records.

text.zh-CN:
产品和场景有助于安排戒烟支持。

- 记录当前使用的产品、每天使用情况、何时开始或停止，以及工作日和休息日差异。
- 记录家中、车内和工作场所是否有人吸烟；只写自己不吸烟会漏掉被动暴露。
text.en:
Products and settings help shape cessation support.

- Record products, usual daily use, starting or stopping dates and differences between workdays and days off.
- Note smoking in the home, car and workplace; personal nonsmoking alone misses passive exposure.

text.zh-CN:
共同建立无烟环境，并为戒烟提供具体帮助。

- 与同住者约定家中及车内无烟；需要时寻求工作场所的无烟保护。
- 想戒烟时联系戒烟服务，讨论咨询与适合的戒烟药物；复吸时调整诱因和支持安排。
text.en:
Build smoke-free environments and practical cessation support.

- Agree on a smoke-free home and car with household members and seek workplace protections where needed.
- Contact cessation services to discuss counselling and appropriate medicines; review triggers and support after a return to use.

text.zh-CN:
戒烟获益证据充分，适合的辅助方式需按个人情况选择。

- 烟草和二手烟没有已知安全暴露水平，减少接触的方向适用于各年龄。
- 记录尼古丁产品不等于否定医疗戒烟方案；处方或药师指导的戒烟辅助应单独与团队核对。
text.en:
Benefits of quitting are well established; support choices depend on circumstances.

- No safe level of tobacco or second-hand smoke exposure is established, so reducing exposure matters across ages.
- Recording nicotine products does not reject medically supported cessation; check prescribed or pharmacist-guided aids with the care team.

title.zh-CN: 酒精及其他非医疗物质使用
title.en: Alcohol and other nonmedical substance use

summary.zh-CN: 记录使用量、频率和失控迹象，把减少伤害与安全求助结合。
summary.en: Record amount, frequency and loss of control, combining harm reduction with safe access to help.

text.zh-CN:
酒精可影响判断和反应，也会造成长期器官伤害。

- 一次大量饮酒会增加交通事故、跌倒和暴力等风险；长期使用与肝病及多种癌症有关。
- 其他非医疗物质及混用情况也应告诉医疗人员，以便评估依赖、相互作用与中毒。
text.en:
Alcohol affects judgement and reactions and can cause lasting organ harm.

- Heavy drinking occasions increase crashes, falls and violence; longer-term use is linked to liver disease and several cancers.
- Tell clinicians about other nonmedical substances and combinations so dependence, interactions and poisoning can be assessed.

text.zh-CN:
饮酒模式和后果同样值得记录。

- 记录一周饮酒天数、每次饮品类型与量、一次大量饮酒和无法按计划停止的情况。
- 记录漏工、受伤、关系冲突、晨起想喝酒或停酒后发抖等变化；各地标准杯容量不同，保留具体饮品信息。
text.en:
Patterns and consequences matter alongside quantity.

- Record days used, drink type and amount, heavy occasions and difficulty stopping as planned.
- Record missed work, injury, relationship conflict, morning drinking or shaking after stopping; standard-drink definitions vary, so keep product details.

text.zh-CN:
从清楚自己的模式和获取支持开始。

- 不饮酒者无需为健康开始饮酒；孕期避免饮酒，驾驶或操作机器时也应避免使用影响清醒的物质。
- 怀疑酒精依赖者先联系医疗人员安排安全戒断，突然自行停酒可能危险；抽搐或严重意识变化应立即急救。
text.en:
Start with a clear picture and support.

- People who do not drink need not start for health; avoid alcohol in pregnancy and avoid substances that impair alertness when driving or operating machinery.
- Suspected alcohol dependence needs a medically planned withdrawal because abrupt unsupported stopping can be dangerous. Seizures or severe changes in awareness need emergency help.

text.zh-CN:
风险随总量、频率、场景和个人状态改变。

- WHO指出没有完全无风险的饮酒形式；这不表示每次少量饮酒都会立即造成疾病。
- 观察到的饮酒与健康关联可能受原有疾病和生活条件影响，不能单凭这类关联认定饮酒有护心作用。
text.en:
Risk changes with amount, pattern, context and individual health.

- WHO states that no drinking pattern is entirely risk-free; this does not mean every small intake immediately causes disease.
- Observed associations can reflect existing illness and circumstances, so they alone do not establish a heart-protective effect of drinking.

summary.zh-CN: 记录实际做了多少活动，逐步安排有氧、肌力和平衡活动。
summary.en: Record activity actually performed and build aerobic, strengthening and balance activities gradually.

text.zh-CN:
活动包括走路、骑行、游戏、家务和运动训练。

- 规律活动帮助心肺、肌肉骨骼及心理健康；久坐描述清醒时长时间低活动的状态。
- 这里记录行为；走得多快、站起是否困难等测得能力，归入“功能储备”。
text.en:
Movement includes walking, cycling, play, household tasks and exercise.

- Regular activity supports cardiovascular, musculoskeletal and mental health; sedentary time describes low-movement waking behaviour.
- This factor records behaviour. Measured ability, such as walking performance or difficulty rising, belongs to functional reserve.

text.zh-CN:
把一周活动拆成可以回顾的记录。

- 记录活动名称、分钟数、每周次数和久坐时段，另记肌力和平衡训练。
- 记录活动时的不适以及需要的辅助或休息，以便选择可持续的强度。
text.en:
Use a weekly record that can be reviewed.

- Note activity, minutes, frequency and prolonged sitting, with separate entries for strengthening and balance work.
- Note discomfort, assistance and rest requirements to choose a sustainable intensity.

text.zh-CN:
从现有能力逐渐增加，分散安排也有价值。

- WHO建议成人每周150–300分钟中等强度或75–150分钟高强度有氧活动，并至少2天肌力训练；65岁及以上再安排每周至少3天侧重平衡和力量的综合活动。
- 5–17岁平均每天至少60分钟中高强度活动，每周至少3天包含较高强度及肌肉、骨骼强化活动。
- 1–2岁每天至少180分钟各类活动；3–4岁同为180分钟，其中至少60分钟较活跃。不能独立移动的婴儿清醒时可分段趴玩，每天合计至少30分钟，并由照护者看护。
text.en:
Build gradually from current ability; shorter periods can contribute.

- WHO advises adults to aim for 150–300 minutes of moderate or 75–150 minutes of vigorous aerobic activity weekly plus strengthening on at least 2 days. Adults aged 65 or over should also include multicomponent balance and strength activity on at least 3 days weekly.
- Ages 5–17 should average at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity daily, with vigorous and muscle/bone-strengthening activities on at least 3 days weekly.
- Ages 1–2 need at least 180 minutes of varied activity daily; ages 3–4 need 180 minutes including at least 60 of more energetic activity. Nonmobile infants can accumulate at least 30 minutes of supervised awake tummy time across the day.

text.zh-CN:
这些是人群活动建议，起步量和活动形式仍需匹配能力。

- 有慢病、残障或较久未活动者，可从能完成的活动开始，必要时获得康复指导。
- 无禁忌的孕产期人群，WHO建议每周至少150分钟中等强度活动；出现不适或产科限制时先核对方案。婴儿趴玩只在清醒时，睡眠仍按安全睡眠安排。
text.en:
These population recommendations allow different starting points and activity forms.

- People with chronic disease, disability or prolonged inactivity can begin with manageable movement and seek rehabilitation guidance as needed.
- For pregnancy and postpartum without contraindications, WHO recommends at least 150 minutes of moderate activity weekly; symptoms or obstetric restrictions require a plan review. Infant tummy time is for waking hours; use safe-sleep arrangements for sleep.

summary.zh-CN: 同时观察睡眠时长、规律、夜间问题和白天功能。
summary.en: Track duration, regularity, night-time problems and daytime functioning together.

text.zh-CN:
充足且有恢复感的睡眠支持注意、情绪和身体调节。

- 同样睡了足够时间，频繁醒来或白天仍困可能提示睡眠质量问题。
- 夜班、时差、疼痛或睡眠疾病会改变作息；找到具体原因有助于选择措施。
text.en:
Adequate refreshing sleep supports attention, mood and bodily regulation.

- Frequent awakenings or daytime sleepiness despite enough hours may indicate poor sleep quality.
- Shift work, time-zone changes, pain or sleep disorders can disrupt the pattern; identifying contributors guides action.

text.zh-CN:
记录上床、入睡、夜醒、起床和白天清醒度。

- CDC参考：0–3个月14–17小时，4–12个月12–16小时，1–2岁11–14小时，3–5岁10–13小时；婴幼儿时长包含午睡。
- 6–12岁9–12小时，13–17岁8–10小时；18–60岁至少7小时，61–64岁7–9小时，65岁及以上7–8小时。
- 同时记录咖啡因、酒精、午睡、打鼾或憋醒；时长达标却仍明显困倦也需要说明。
text.en:
Record bedtime, estimated onset, awakenings, rising time and daytime alertness.

- CDC references are 14–17 hours at 0–3 months, 12–16 at 4–12 months, 11–14 at 1–2 years and 10–13 at 3–5 years; young-child totals include naps.
- Ages 6–12: 9–12 hours; 13–17: 8–10; 18–60: at least 7; 61–64: 7–9; age 65 or over: 7–8.
- Also record caffeine, alcohol, naps, snoring or gasping. Marked sleepiness despite meeting the time reference remains relevant.

title.zh-CN: 把作息和症状一起调整

text.zh-CN:
从固定节律和睡眠环境开始。

- 尽量保持相近的起床时间，让卧室安静、舒适，观察晚间咖啡因、酒精和大餐是否干扰睡眠。
- 持续睡不好、频繁憋醒或白天困到影响安全时，应就诊；助眠药与慢性失眠治疗详见失眠正文。
text.en:
Begin with regular timing and a supportive environment.

- Keep rising time reasonably consistent and the bedroom quiet and comfortable; review late caffeine, alcohol and large meals.
- Persistent sleep problems, frequent gasping or sleepiness that compromises safety calls for assessment. See the insomnia article for treatment and sleep medicines.

text.zh-CN:
年龄范围用于安排睡眠机会，仍需结合恢复感和功能。

- 不能把每晚偶尔偏离参考范围当作疾病；持续影响学习、工作或安全更值得评估。
- 长睡眠与死亡的观察性关联可能反映其他健康问题；应评估困倦或睡眠变化的原因，而不是据此强行少睡。
text.en:
Age ranges help plan sleep opportunity alongside restoration and function.

- An occasional night outside a reference range is not itself a disorder; sustained effects on study, work or safety deserve assessment.
- Observed links between long sleep and mortality may reflect other health problems; assess the cause of sleepiness or changed sleep rather than forcing less sleep on that basis.

summary.zh-CN: 关注吸入的空气和暴露场景，用环境改善与活动安排减少暴露。
summary.en: Consider inhaled air and exposure settings, using cleaner environments and adapted routines.

text.zh-CN:
空气中的细颗粒和气体可影响心肺健康。

- PM2.5指直径不超过2.5微米的细颗粒，可深入肺部；长期暴露与呼吸和心血管损伤有关。
- 交通、工业和家庭燃烧都可能是来源，室内与室外暴露需要一起考虑。
text.en:
Fine particles and gases can affect cardiovascular and respiratory health.

- PM2.5 means particles no larger than 2.5 micrometres, capable of reaching deep into the lungs; long-term exposure contributes to respiratory and cardiovascular harm.
- Traffic, industry and household combustion can all contribute, so consider both indoor and outdoor exposure.

text.zh-CN:
空气质量数据描述环境，不是个人疾病检验。

- 查看当地可靠空气质量监测、污染物类型与平均时间；小时读数和全年均值不能直接当成同一指标。
- WHO 2021年PM2.5年均指导值为5微克/立方米，用于长期空气质量改善，不是超过一次就中毒的界线。
text.en:
Air data describe the environment rather than diagnosing a person.

- Use reliable local monitoring and check pollutant and averaging time; hourly readings and annual averages are different measures.
- The WHO 2021 annual PM2.5 guideline is 5 micrograms per cubic metre, a long-term air-quality aim rather than a threshold for poisoning after one exceedance.

text.zh-CN:
把个人安排和环境治理结合。

- 减少室内烟雾和污染燃烧，推动更清洁的做饭、取暖与交通条件；家庭烟草暴露见对应因素。
- 污染较重时按当地预警调整户外活动的时段与地点；已有哮喘等疾病者按既定症状计划处理变化。
text.en:
Combine daily choices with cleaner surroundings.

- Reduce indoor smoke and polluting combustion and seek cleaner cooking, heating and transport; household tobacco is addressed in its own factor.
- Follow local alerts to adapt the time and place of outdoor activity during pollution episodes; people with asthma or other illness should follow their symptom plan.

text.zh-CN:
健康指导值服务于减少整个人群的长期暴露。

- 不同地区污染混合物与暴露持续时间不同，不能把一项国外队列的死亡比例换算成个人寿命。
text.en:
Guidelines support lower long-term population exposure.

- Pollutant mixtures and duration differ by place, so a mortality association from one foreign cohort cannot determine an individual lifespan.

title.zh-CN: 铅、一氧化碳与有毒暴露
title.en: Lead, carbon monoxide and toxic exposures

summary.zh-CN: 先识别接触来源和场景，再按具体物质选择检测与处理。
summary.en: Identify the substance and setting before choosing tests and exposure control.

text.zh-CN:
暴露可能来自家庭、工作或带回家的污染。

- 铅会影响儿童神经发育，污染尘土、含铅材料或成人工作中的污染可成为来源。
- 一氧化碳是无色无味气体，燃烧设备使用不当可迅速造成严重中毒，不能靠嗅觉判断安全。
text.en:
Exposure may originate at home, work or from contamination carried home.

- Lead can harm children’s neurological development; contaminated dust, lead-containing materials and workplace contamination are possible sources.
- Carbon monoxide is colourless and odourless; unsafe combustion can cause severe poisoning rapidly, so smell cannot establish safety.

text.zh-CN:
记录接触史，按风险选检查。

- 说明产品、工种、装修、饮水或反复接触情况；儿童疑似铅暴露时请医生判断血铅检查。
- CDC儿童血铅参考值为3.5微克/分升，用于识别需进一步控制暴露的人群；低于它也不代表已知安全。
text.en:
Use exposure history to guide testing.

- Describe products, work, renovation, water and repeated contact; clinicians can assess the need for a child’s blood lead test.
- The CDC childhood reference value is 3.5 micrograms per decilitre, identifying children for further exposure control; a lower result does not establish a safe level.

title.zh-CN: 停止来源比反复检测重要

text.zh-CN:
让检测结果落实为环境改变。

- 发现儿童血铅升高时，与医疗和公共卫生团队查找来源并安排复测、营养与发育评估，避免自行使用排毒产品。
- 安装并维护一氧化碳报警器；发电机不得在室内或车库运行。怀疑一氧化碳中毒时立即到新鲜空气处并求急救，不回到危险空间。
text.en:
Turn a result into exposure control.

- For elevated childhood blood lead, work with clinical and public-health teams on source investigation, repeat testing, nutrition and development; avoid self-directed detox products.
- Install and maintain carbon monoxide alarms and never run generators indoors or in garages. If poisoning is suspected, move to fresh air and seek emergency help without returning to the hazardous space.

title.en: A reference is not a safe limit

text.zh-CN:
每种物质需要对应的评估方法。

- 3.5微克/分升来自美国儿童血铅分布，是公共卫生行动参考；本地检测与后续服务按当地程序。
- 铅、一氧化碳和其他职业化学品的检测与处理方式不同，应根据具体接触史选择检查。
text.en:
Assessment depends on the specific substance.

- The 3.5-microgram-per-decilitre value derives from the US child blood-lead distribution; local testing and follow-up follow local services.
- Testing and treatment differ for lead, carbon monoxide and occupational chemicals, so assessment should follow the specific exposure history.

summary.zh-CN: 减少交通、居家和高温环境中可以改变的伤害机会。
summary.en: Reduce modifiable injury hazards in transport, homes and heat.

text.zh-CN:
环境保护可以在失误或身体状态变化时减少伤害。

- 安全带、儿童约束装置及合适头盔是交通保护的一部分，还需要安全速度和道路设计。
- 高温妨碍散热并增加身体负担；清晰走道、照明与扶手可减少绊倒环境。
text.en:
Environmental protection reduces harm when mistakes or health changes occur.

- Seatbelts, child restraints and suitable helmets contribute to road safety alongside safe speed and road design.
- Heat impairs cooling and strains the body; clear routes, lighting and rails reduce household trip hazards.

text.zh-CN:
用具体清单记录风险出现在哪里。

- 记录常走路线、车辆保护装置、家中易滑或绊倒处，以及高温期间能否进入凉爽空间。
- 婴儿睡眠空间应单独检查：仰卧、独立且硬平的床面、没有松软被褥和玩具。
text.en:
Use a practical list of where hazards occur.

- Review travel routes, protective equipment, slippery or cluttered areas and access to a cool space during heat.
- Check infant sleep separately: back sleeping, a separate firm flat surface and no loose bedding or soft toys.

text.zh-CN:
把保护措施变成每次都会执行的安排。

- 乘车使用适合的约束装置，骑行使用合适头盔；清理走道、改善夜间照明并在需要处加扶手。
- 高温时调整劳作和外出安排，定时联系独居或行动不便者；不要将儿童留在停驶车辆内。
text.en:
Make protection part of each routine.

- Use suitable vehicle restraints and helmets for riding; clear routes, improve night lighting and add rails where needed.
- Adapt work and outings during heat and check on people living alone or with limited mobility; never leave children in parked vehicles.

title.zh-CN: 能力与环境共同决定安全
title.en: Safety depends on ability and environment

text.zh-CN:
同一环境对不同能力的人影响不同。

- 高龄、残障、照护需求或慢病会改变保护需求；跌倒后的功能评估放在功能储备因素中。
- 发生事故之前即可改善危险场景；照明、护栏和适合的保护装置可让日常活动更安全。
text.en:
The same setting affects people differently.

- Age, disability, care needs and chronic illness change protection needs; assessment after falls belongs to functional reserve.
- Hazards can be reduced before an accident; lighting, rails and suitable protective equipment can make daily activities safer.

summary.zh-CN: 识别食物、住房、教育、工作和照护资源的实际障碍。
summary.en: Identify practical barriers involving food, housing, education, work and support resources.

text.zh-CN:
生活条件决定哪些健康选择真正做得到。

- 食物和住房不稳定会影响营养、休息和暴露环境；缺少交通或请假机会也可能延误照护。
- 收入、教育和歧视影响获得机会与支持的方式，许多问题需要社区和制度共同解决。
text.en:
Living conditions determine which healthy choices are feasible.

- Food or housing insecurity affects nutrition, rest and exposure; transport or leave barriers may delay care.
- Income, education and discrimination shape opportunities and support, often requiring community and policy action.

text.zh-CN:
用能回答的实际问题整理需求。

- 是否担心食物不够、房租或住房不稳、家中难以保温降温，或照护者无法休息？
- 是否因费用、语言、交通或工作时间难以获得帮助？这里记录资源条件，实际医疗服务使用归入“医疗服务”。
text.en:
Organise needs with practical questions.

- Is food running short, housing unstable, heating or cooling inadequate, or a caregiver unable to rest?
- Do cost, language, transport or working hours obstruct help? Record these resource barriers here and actual care use under medical access.

text.zh-CN:
先选择影响最大的现实障碍。

- 向基层医疗或社会服务说明具体困难，了解可用的食物、住房、交通、照护或翻译支持。
- 社区和机构可改善无障碍空间、工作条件及资源转介；个人健康计划也应适应现有条件。
text.en:
Start with the barrier making the greatest practical difference.

- Describe specific difficulties to primary care or social services and ask about food, housing, transport, caregiving or language support.
- Communities and institutions can improve accessibility, working conditions and referrals; personal care plans should fit actual circumstances.

title.zh-CN: 群体关联不是个人标签
title.en: Population patterns are not personal labels

text.zh-CN:
社会不平等与健康的关系有广泛人口证据。

- 这些因素常同时影响多种暴露，不能把贫困、饮食和医疗延误的风险简单相加。
- 评估重点是当前可改善的安全与资源需要，例如食物、住房、照护和获得帮助的障碍。
text.en:
Population evidence links social inequality and health.

- These factors often affect several exposures at once, so poverty, diet and delayed-care risks cannot simply be added.
- Assessment focuses on current, changeable safety and resource needs such as food, housing, care and barriers to support.

summary.zh-CN: 利用接种记录确认按当地程序应完成的保护。
summary.en: Use vaccination records to identify protection due under the local schedule.

text.zh-CN:
疫苗帮助免疫系统学习识别特定病原体。

- 之后遇到相关感染时，身体更容易作出防御；不同疫苗可降低患病或重症风险。
- 一些人因年龄、免疫状态或特定过敏无法接种某种疫苗，也需要周围人和环境的保护。
text.en:
Vaccines train the immune system to recognise particular pathogens.

- Later exposure can meet a prepared response; vaccines differ in protection against infection or severe illness.
- Age, immune status or particular allergies can prevent someone receiving a specific vaccine, making protection around them relevant too.

text.zh-CN:
记录疫苗名称、日期和已完成剂次。

- 带既往纸质或电子记录核对漏种和下一次时间，记录接种后曾发生的明显反应。
- 迁居、旅行、怀孕、进入照护机构或免疫状态改变时，重新核对适用程序。
text.en:
Record product, dates and completed doses.

- Bring paper or electronic records to check missing doses and what is due next, including significant previous reactions.
- Review eligibility when moving, travelling, becoming pregnant, entering care or changing immune status.

text.zh-CN:
向当地接种服务确认适合的疫苗和时间。

- 儿童、成人和老年人按所在地区的年龄及风险建议接种，不用一个全球固定清单覆盖所有人。
- 先说明既往严重过敏、妊娠和影响免疫的治疗，让接种人员决定是否调整种类或时机。
text.en:
Confirm appropriate products and timing with local vaccination services.

- Children, adults and older people follow local age- and risk-based advice rather than one worldwide fixed list.
- Explain severe previous allergies, pregnancy and immune-affecting treatment so staff can adjust the product or timing when needed.

text.zh-CN:
疫苗有广泛疾病预防证据，效果与病原体、产品和人群有关。

- 完成接种后仍可能感染；出现明显病情变化时按相应病症的就医条件行动。
text.en:
Vaccines have broad preventive evidence, with effects varying by pathogen, product and population.

- Infection can still occur after vaccination; important clinical deterioration requires the relevant condition’s care advice.

title.zh-CN: 医疗服务使用与连续照护
title.en: Use of medical services and continuity of care

summary.zh-CN: 关注需要的预防、治疗和康复是否及时完成并获得后续结果。
summary.en: Track whether needed prevention, treatment and rehabilitation happen promptly and receive follow-through.

text.zh-CN:
健康服务从预防延伸到治疗、康复和生活质量支持。

- 一次开单不等于检查结果已解释；发现异常后能完成复诊和必要转诊，才形成连续照护。
- 资源是否可获得归入社会资源；这里关注实际预约、获得服务和后续处理。
text.en:
Health services span prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and support for quality of life.

- Ordering a test is different from explaining its result; follow-up and indicated referrals complete the pathway after an abnormal finding.
- Availability of resources belongs to social resources; this factor follows appointments, care received and subsequent action.

text.zh-CN:
建立简短的检查与随访清单。

- 记录约定检查、完成日期、结果是否解读以及下一步由谁负责；出院后明确复诊和药物清单。
- 筛查按年龄、家族史、既往结果及当地建议安排，不把所有检查设为所有年龄每年必做。
text.en:
Use a short testing and follow-up list.

- Record planned tests, completion, whether results were discussed and who owns the next step; clarify review and medicines after discharge.
- Screening follows age, family history, prior results and local advice instead of universal annual testing at every age.

text.zh-CN:
让照护安排清晰到可以执行。

- 就诊时带重要病史、报告和用药记录，离开前确认何时复查、哪些变化需提前联系。
- 孕期尽早建立产前照护；WHO模型建议至少8次产前接触，首次在孕12周内，并包含实际评估和支持。
text.en:
Make the care plan actionable.

- Bring important history, results and medicines, and confirm the review date and changes that warrant earlier contact.
- Establish antenatal care early. The WHO model recommends at least 8 contacts, starting within 12 weeks, with assessment and support rather than attendance alone.

title.en: Quality matters more than test counts

text.zh-CN:
有用的服务要符合需要并能接上后续处理。

- 医疗、康复和缓和医疗都可能有价值，选择取决于病情、功能和个人目标。
- WHO产前接触是全球照护框架；高风险妊娠可能需更多接触，具体检查和转诊按当地安排。
text.en:
Useful services fit the need and connect to follow-up.

- Treatment, rehabilitation and palliative care can all contribute, depending on illness, function and personal goals.
- WHO antenatal contacts are a global care framework; higher-risk pregnancies may need more, with tests and referrals arranged locally.

summary.zh-CN: 关注持续困扰、生活功能与认知变化，尽早获得适合的支持。
summary.en: Notice persistent distress, functioning and cognitive changes, and obtain appropriate support.

text.zh-CN:
心理健康影响应对压力、学习、工作与关系。

- 困扰可能涉及生物、心理和社会因素，表现也不只是不开心，可包括焦虑、睡眠和日常能力变化。
- 认知包括记忆、注意和处理事情的能力；突然改变与长期逐渐变化需要不同的处理速度。
text.en:
Mental health affects coping, learning, work and relationships.

- Biological, psychological and social influences can produce anxiety, sleep changes and impaired functioning as well as low mood.
- Cognition includes memory, attention and handling tasks; sudden change and gradual change require different urgency.

text.zh-CN:
记录持续多久、出现在哪些场景和影响什么。

- 描述上学、工作、进食、自我照顾或社交是否变困难，也说明睡眠、药物和物质使用变化。
- 量表可以帮助沟通症状，但需要访谈和背景解释；不把一个分数单独当作确诊。
text.en:
Describe duration, setting and practical effects.

- Note difficulty with school, work, eating, self-care or social life, together with sleep, medicine and substance-use changes.
- Questionnaires can support communication but require clinical discussion and context rather than diagnosis from a score alone.

text.zh-CN:
持续影响生活的变化值得安排评估。

- 可先联系基层医疗或心理服务，带上具体例子，讨论适合的心理与社会支持；诊疗细节见抑郁和焦虑正文。
- 有伤害自己或他人的即时危险时，联系当地急救或危机服务并寻求可信任者陪伴；突然意识混乱也需紧急医疗评估。
text.en:
Arrange assessment when changes persistently affect life.

- Primary care or mental-health services can review examples and agree psychological and social support; use depression and anxiety articles for clinical detail.
- Immediate danger of harm to self or others needs local emergency or crisis help and support from a trusted person. Sudden confusion also needs urgent medical assessment.

text.zh-CN:
心理困扰、认知下降和社会孤立可以相互影响，但不是同一指标。

- 持续记忆或处理事务能力变化，应考虑身体病、药物和感觉障碍等背景，由专业评估明确原因。
text.en:
Distress, cognitive decline and isolation can interact but measure different things.

- Persistent memory or task difficulties need assessment in the context of illness, medicines and sensory problems.

summary.zh-CN: 区分与人接触少、感到孤独，以及能否获得可信任的支持。
summary.en: Distinguish limited contact, loneliness and access to trusted support.

text.zh-CN:
社交人数并不能完全说明一个人获得了多少支持。

- 社会孤立是角色、关系或接触较少的客观状态；孤独是实际关系与自己需要的关系不匹配带来的痛苦感受。
- 关系的质量也重要：有人可求助、相处是否安全和支持，都影响联结的价值。
text.en:
The number of contacts does not fully describe support.

- Social isolation is objectively limited roles, relationships or contact; loneliness is distress when actual relationships do not meet a person’s needs.
- Quality matters too: available help and safe, supportive interactions shape the value of a connection.

text.zh-CN:
记录接触方式和是否满足需要。

- 可以回顾最近一周与谁联系、是否有愿意求助的人，以及身体或交通问题是否妨碍见面。
- 也问是否经常感到孤独、关系紧张或不安全；独居本身不能替代这些问题。
text.en:
Record contact patterns and whether they meet needs.

- Review recent contact, whom you would ask for help and whether health or transport obstructs meeting people.
- Also ask about loneliness, strain or unsafe relationships; living alone does not answer all these questions.

text.zh-CN:
选择自己愿意并能持续参加的联系。

- 安排固定但可接受的通话、探访或共同活动，可通过兴趣、志愿服务或社区小组建立联系。
- 听力、行动、交通或数字使用困难时，先改善进入活动的条件；照护者也需要自己的支持机会。
text.en:
Choose contact that is wanted and manageable.

- Arrange acceptable regular calls, visits or shared activities; interests, volunteering or community groups can offer connections.
- Address hearing, mobility, transport or digital-access barriers first; caregivers need support opportunities too.

title.zh-CN: 关联不能变成社交配额
title.en: Associations are not a social quota

text.zh-CN:
社会联结与健康有关，干预要尊重个人需要。

- 联系次数、支持功能和关系质量是不同维度；强迫增加人数未必解决孤独。
- 联系安排应符合本人的意愿、实际需要和关系质量，可以随身体状态与生活条件调整。
text.en:
Social connection relates to health, while support should fit individual needs.

- Frequency, practical support and relationship quality differ; forcing more contacts may not resolve loneliness.
- Contact plans should fit the person’s wishes, needs and relationship quality and can change with health and circumstances.

summary.zh-CN: 观察真实完成日常活动的能力，以及受到疾病或跌倒影响后的恢复。
summary.en: Observe real daily abilities and recovery after illness or falls.

text.zh-CN:
功能储备是身体和心理应对日常需要及打击的余地。

- 肌力、平衡、步行、视听力与认知共同影响能否买菜、洗澡、走动和沟通。
- 年龄相同的人能力可能差异很大；辅助器具和合适环境也能帮助维持生活能力。
text.en:
Reserve is the capacity to meet daily demands and cope with setbacks.

- Strength, balance, walking, vision, hearing and cognition affect shopping, washing, mobility and communication.
- People of the same age can have very different abilities; aids and supportive settings can maintain function.

title.zh-CN: 测能力而不重复计活动
title.en: Measure ability rather than activity volume

text.zh-CN:
看与自己以往状态相比发生了什么变化。

- 记录跌倒和差点跌倒、从椅子站起或走路是否更困难，以及购物、做饭和管理日常事务是否需要更多帮助。
- 专业评估可使用步行、椅子起立或平衡测试，并检查视听力；这里记录测得结果，运动分钟数放在身体活动因素。
text.en:
Compare current ability with the person’s previous baseline.

- Record falls and near-falls, difficulty rising or walking, and increased help with shopping, cooking or everyday tasks.
- Professional assessment may use walking, chair-rise or balance tests and sensory checks; activity minutes belong to the physical-activity factor.

text.zh-CN:
把新出现的困难带到医疗或康复评估中。

- 反复跌倒、走动减少或看听不清时，评估身体、感觉及环境因素，安排合适的训练和辅助设备。
- 发生跌倒后也检查相关用药，具体药物复核见药物安全；家中照明和通道修改见安全环境。
text.en:
Bring new difficulties to clinical or rehabilitation assessment.

- Recurrent falls, reduced mobility or vision/hearing problems call for assessment of physical, sensory and environmental contributors and appropriate training or aids.
- After falls, include a medicine review under medication safety; lighting and route changes are covered under safe environments.

title.zh-CN: 结果以个人生活目标衡量

text.zh-CN:
功能评估用于决定支持，而非以年龄给人贴标签。

- 例如能否安全起床、听清谈话、出门购物，可以作为复评时可比较的目标。
- 听力处理的目标包括改善沟通与日常生活，应观察这些实际功能是否改善。
text.en:
Functional assessment guides support rather than labelling by age.

- Safe transfers, hearing a conversation or shopping outside can provide comparable goals at reassessment.
- Hearing care aims to improve communication and daily life; follow whether these practical functions improve.

summary.zh-CN: 用完整清单核对每种药的用途、实际服法和不良反应。
summary.en: Use a complete list to review each medicine’s purpose, actual use and unwanted effects.

text.zh-CN:
药物可预防或治疗疾病，也可能产生相互作用。

- 处方药、非处方药、草药和补充剂都要一起看；由不同医生开药并不保证相互作用已被发现。
- 老年人常同时治疗多种问题，嗜睡、头晕等反应可能影响驾驶、跌倒和日常功能。
text.en:
Medicines can prevent or treat disease while also interacting.

- Review prescriptions, over-the-counter products, herbs and supplements together; separate prescribers may not see the full combination.
- Older adults often receive treatment for several conditions, and drowsiness or dizziness can affect driving, falls and daily function.

text.zh-CN:
记录实际怎么用，而不只是处方上写了什么。

- 列出名称、用途、服用时间、实际用量、开药者和过敏反应，包括偶尔才用的药。
- 记录开始、停止或换药后出现的头晕、困倦、出血等变化，复诊时带药盒或清单核对。
text.en:
Record actual use rather than the prescription alone.

- List name, purpose, timing, amount actually used, prescriber and allergies, including occasional products.
- Record dizziness, sleepiness, bleeding or other changes after starting, stopping or switching products, and bring the list or containers to review.

text.zh-CN:
新增药物和照护转换时，确认整套方案。

- 出院、换医生或加用非处方药时，请医生或药师核对重复成分、相互作用和仍需继续的药。
- 漏服、停药或难以吞咽时询问具体药物的处理方式；不要把一种药的停用办法套到其他药，也不要自行借用他人处方。
text.en:
Check the full regimen when treatment or care changes.

- After discharge, changing clinicians or adding an over-the-counter product, review duplicate ingredients, interactions and ongoing need with a clinician or pharmacist.
- Ask for medicine-specific advice about missed doses, stopping or swallowing difficulties; do not generalise one drug’s instructions or borrow prescriptions.

text.zh-CN:
药物数量本身不能说明方案好坏。

- 多药可能都有必要，也可能存在已经不需要或相互冲突的项目；复核要逐项看用途、效果和风险。
- 调整或停用药物前，结合具体药物、病情和不良反应与医生或药师核对；各病症正文解释对应药物角色。
text.en:
The medicine count alone does not determine quality.

- Several medicines may all be necessary, or some may no longer help or may conflict; review purpose, benefit and risk for each.
- Before changing or stopping treatment, review the particular medicine, condition and adverse effects with a clinician or pharmacist; disease articles explain specific medicine roles.

intro.zh-CN: 本阶段重点是喂养、发育、安全和预防照护的连续性，由照护者协助记录与行动。
intro.en: Stage priorities include feeding, development, safety and continuity of preventive care, with caregivers supporting records and actions.

text.zh-CN:
把孩子的变化与实际照护一起观察。

- 保留出生和儿童保健记录，特别说明早产或新生儿治疗经历，让儿科据此安排发育与喂养随访。
- 观察玩耍、学习、说话、互动和移动能力；记录已经会做的事情，方便发现进展与变化。
- 照护者交接时说明喂养、睡眠空间和已完成接种；具体指标查看下方关联因素。
text.en:
Observe development alongside caregiving.

- Keep birth and child-health records, especially prematurity or neonatal treatment, so paediatric follow-up can address feeding and development.
- Observe play, learning, speech, interaction and movement, recording established skills to make change visible.
- At caregiver handovers, clarify feeding, the sleep setting and completed vaccinations; detailed measures are in the linked factors.

text.zh-CN:
早发现困难，可以更早接上评估和支持。

- 担心孩子没有达到相应发育表现或失去已经获得的技能时，及时联系儿科，描述具体变化并询问发育评估。
- 持续喂养困难或生长停滞时，带喂养和生长记录求助，不自行照搬成人限制饮食。
- 对照护安全或家庭资源有困难时，主动提出需要的实际帮助，例如接种交通、食物和安全睡眠空间。
text.en:
Early recognition helps connect assessment and support.

- For concern about development or loss of established skills, contact paediatric care promptly, describe examples and ask about developmental assessment.
- Persistent feeding difficulty or faltering growth needs review with feeding and growth records, without adult-style dietary restriction.
- Describe practical safety or resource needs such as transport to vaccination, food and a safe sleep space.

intro.zh-CN: 本阶段重点是把健康安排融入家庭与学校，并让儿童和青少年逐渐表达自己的需要。
intro.en: Stage priorities include integrating health into home and school life and helping children and adolescents express their needs.

text.zh-CN:
关注生长与功能轨迹，也关注环境是否支持。

- 记录成长、活动和睡眠时，结合学习、同伴互动和兴趣参与；避免只根据体重评价孩子。
- 为日常玩耍和运动提供安全机会；学校与家庭可协调作息和需要的照护支持。
- 用适龄方式讨论烟草、电子烟、酒精和网络关系，了解实际接触及同伴压力。
text.en:
Follow growth and functioning alongside environmental support.

- Consider learning, peers and interests with growth, activity and sleep rather than judging a child by weight alone.
- Provide safe daily play and movement; home and school can coordinate routines and care support.
- Discuss tobacco, vaping, alcohol and online relationships in age-appropriate ways, including actual exposure and peer pressure.

text.zh-CN:
持续影响学习、生活或安全的情况应得到回应。

- 明显持续退缩、情绪困扰或日常能力下降时，与孩子及可信任的照护者讨论，并联系适龄健康服务。
- 遭受暴力或有即时自伤危险时，先安排安全并联系当地紧急或保护服务。
- 反复看听不清或体力活动明显受限时，安排相应检查，让学习和活动支持跟上需要。
text.en:
Respond to persistent effects on learning, daily life or safety.

- Discuss sustained withdrawal, distress or reduced functioning with the young person and trusted caregivers and contact age-appropriate services.
- For violence or immediate self-harm danger, establish safety and contact local emergency or protection services.
- Repeated hearing or vision difficulty or substantial activity limitation warrants assessment and appropriate school or activity support.

intro.zh-CN: 工作、迁移、家庭和生育计划常在此阶段改变，重点是建立能持续执行的健康安排。
intro.en: Work, moves, family life and reproductive plans often change; stage priorities include building routines and care that can continue.

title.zh-CN: 让健康记录跟随生活变化

text.zh-CN:
先建立能带到不同医疗机构的核心资料。

- 整理家族史、接种记录、主要检查结果与用药，迁居或换医生时带上。
- 根据家族早发病、既往异常及当前症状商定检查；短期没有症状不能代替风险评估。
- 夜班、照护或经济压力妨碍行动时，选择可执行的调整，并把障碍告诉医疗团队。
text.en:
Create a core record that can move between services.

- Keep family history, vaccinations, important results and medicines available when moving or changing clinicians.
- Agree testing based on early family disease, previous abnormalities and symptoms; absence of symptoms is not a risk assessment.
- When shift work, caregiving or financial strain obstructs plans, choose feasible changes and explain barriers to the team.

text.zh-CN:
生活转换时也要检查是否遗漏了照护。

- 准备怀孕或发现怀孕时，叠加孕产期路径，核对原有疾病、药物与产前服务。
- 检查异常之后明确复查和结果解释由谁负责；持续身心不适影响工作或自我照顾时提前就诊。
- 疼痛、呼吸或意识发生急性严重变化时，按对应病症危险信号求助，不等待例行体检。
text.en:
Review care gaps during transitions.

- Add the pregnancy pathway when planning or identifying pregnancy, reviewing existing illness, medicines and antenatal access.
- After abnormal testing, identify who will review the result; seek earlier care when physical or mental symptoms impair work or self-care.
- Acute severe changes in pain, breathing or awareness require the relevant condition’s urgent-care advice rather than a routine checkup.

intro.zh-CN: 本阶段重点是把多年指标与生活暴露联系起来，同时维持工作、照护和日常功能。
intro.en: Stage priorities include reviewing long-term measures and exposures while maintaining work, caregiving and daily function.

text.zh-CN:
重视趋势与可持续方案。

- 带历次血压、血脂或血糖结果评估变化，结合家族史与既往疾病商定随访。
- 筛查项目按当地年龄、性别相关器官、家族史和既往结果安排，避免只做检测却没有后续解释。
- 工作与照护负担较重时，把活动、进餐、睡眠和复诊安排成能执行的日程。
text.en:
Prioritise trends and a sustainable plan.

- Review prior pressure, lipid and glucose results with family history and existing disease to agree follow-up.
- Arrange screening according to local age, relevant anatomy, family history and prior results, including explanation and follow-up.
- Fit movement, meals, sleep and reviews around realistic work and caregiving demands.

title.zh-CN: 治疗与生活功能一起复评

text.zh-CN:
稳定管理也要响应新变化。

- 新增药物或长期不适影响工作和活动时，记录变化并复核治疗组合，避免漏报非处方药。
- 持续胸痛、突然单侧无力或明显意识变化需要紧急处理；健康指标过去正常也不能替代本次评估。
- 定期回顾未完成的转诊、筛查或康复安排，处理费用、交通或照护时间障碍。
text.en:
Respond to new changes even during stable management.

- Record new medicines or symptoms affecting work and activity and review the full regimen, including nonprescription products.
- Persistent chest pain, sudden one-sided weakness or major changes in awareness require urgent care; past normal results do not settle a new event.
- Review unfinished referrals, screening and rehabilitation and address cost, transport or caregiving barriers.

intro.zh-CN: 本阶段重点是同时关注疾病控制和能否完成重视的日常活动，尽早发现可处理的功能变化。
intro.en: Stage priorities include combining disease control with valued daily activities and identifying treatable functional changes early.

text.zh-CN:
让身体状态和照护环境一起进入讨论。

- 记录出门、站起、走路、听清对话和处理家务是否更困难，带具体例子参加复诊。
- 跌倒或差点跌倒后，说明场景、当时感觉与用药变化，让团队同时评估身体和环境。
- 保持愿意参加的联系与活动，听视力、交通或照护障碍可单独请求支持。
text.en:
Discuss health alongside the care environment.

- Record increasing difficulty going out, rising, walking, hearing conversation or managing household tasks and bring examples to review.
- After a fall or near-fall, describe the setting, symptoms and medicine changes so both personal and environmental factors can be assessed.
- Maintain wanted connections and activities, seeking specific help for sensory, transport or care barriers.

text.zh-CN:
新困难可能需要调整支持或治疗。

- 反复跌倒、明显无意消瘦或日常自理变差时，安排评估并检查饮食、疾病和用药原因。
- 站起头晕或治疗后乏力影响行走时，提前联系医疗团队核对目标和耐受，而不是自行减药。
- 突然意识混乱、说话或单侧活动异常，应紧急就医，不能归为年龄增长。
text.en:
New difficulties can call for adapted support or treatment.

- Recurrent falls, marked unintentional weight loss or poorer self-care warrants assessment of nutrition, illness and medicines.
- Standing dizziness or treatment-related weakness affecting walking needs an earlier target and tolerability review rather than self-reducing medicine.
- Sudden confusion, speech difficulty or one-sided weakness needs emergency assessment rather than attribution to age.

title.zh-CN: 85岁及以上：保留能力与生活质量
title.en: Ages 85+: preserve ability and quality of life

intro.zh-CN: 本阶段重点是根据个人能力、意愿和照护支持安排计划；年龄本身不能代替功能评估。
intro.en: Stage priorities include planning around ability, preferences and care support; age alone does not replace functional assessment.

title.zh-CN: 明确本人最看重的目标
title.en: Clarify what matters to the person

text.zh-CN:
以实际生活目标组织照护。

- 讨论最想保留的能力，例如舒适进食、安全转移、沟通或与家人相处，并说明需要的帮助。
- 复诊时一起核对吞咽进食、移动、感觉、情绪及照护者负担，减少多个方案相互冲突。
- 将检查和治疗的预期收益、负担与个人目标一起讨论；康复和舒适照护可以按需要同时提供。
text.en:
Organise care around practical priorities.

- Discuss valued abilities such as comfortable eating, safe transfers, communication or family contact, including needed help.
- Review eating, mobility, senses, mood and caregiver burden together to reduce conflicting plans.
- Discuss expected benefits and burdens of tests and treatment against personal goals; rehabilitation and comfort-focused care can both contribute.

title.zh-CN: 变化时尽早联系照护团队
title.en: Contact the team when needs change

text.zh-CN:
持续稳定的支持也要能处理突然变化。

- 短时间明显少吃、活动减少或照护需求增加时，联系团队寻找原因并调整支持，不仅记录为衰老。
- 发生跌倒或药物后明显困倦头晕时，安排功能和用药复评；突然意识混乱需急救评估。
- 把紧急联系人、主要病史和当前药物清单放在容易取得的位置，并让照护者知道已有照护安排。
text.en:
Stable support should still respond to sudden change.

- A marked short-term drop in intake or activity or increased care needs calls for assessment and support adjustment, rather than recording ageing alone.
- Falls or pronounced medicine-related sleepiness or dizziness call for functional and medication review; sudden confusion needs emergency assessment.
- Keep emergency contacts, major history and current medicines accessible, and ensure caregivers know the agreed care arrangements.

intro.zh-CN: 此路径叠加在实际年龄阶段上，重点关注母体变化、胎儿发育及产后连续照护。
intro.en: Apply this pathway alongside the actual age stage, with priorities including maternal change, fetal development and continuity after birth.

text.zh-CN:
从准备怀孕到产后，安排会随阶段改变。

- 准备或发现怀孕时，带现用药、既往妊娠和慢病资料联系团队；叶酸、活动和接触次数参照关联因素中的适用建议。
- 产检中说明血压、血糖、进食、心理或家庭支持变化，按约完成检查并确认结果。
- 产后继续连接产科、基层医疗和需要的心理支持；照护母亲与婴儿需要同时安排。
text.en:
Plans change from pregnancy preparation through postpartum.

- When planning or identifying pregnancy, bring medicines, previous pregnancy and chronic-disease history; linked factors contain applicable folic acid, activity and care-contact advice.
- Report changes in pressure, glucose, eating, mental health or home support during antenatal care, and complete tests with result review.
- After birth, maintain connections with maternity, primary care and needed psychological support, arranging care for both parent and infant.

title.zh-CN: 需要立即求医的孕产变化

text.zh-CN:
孕期及产后一年内出现严重警示变化，应立即求医。

- 持续或加重的严重头痛、视力变化、胸痛或呼吸困难，立即联系急救或紧急产科服务。
- 妊娠中明显胎动减少、阴道流血或漏液，或产后大量出血，应立即联系医疗服务，不等下一次产检。
- 有伤害自己或婴儿的想法时，立即向医疗或危机服务求助并请可信任者陪伴；告诉接诊人员当前怀孕或距分娩多久。
text.en:
Seek immediate care for urgent warning changes during pregnancy and in the year after delivery.

- Persistent or worsening severe headache, vision changes, chest pain or breathing difficulty requires emergency or urgent maternity care.
- Markedly reduced fetal movement, vaginal bleeding or leaking fluid during pregnancy, or heavy postpartum bleeding requires immediate contact rather than waiting for the next appointment.
- Thoughts of harming yourself or the baby require immediate clinical or crisis help and support from a trusted person; tell the clinician about pregnancy or how long ago the birth occurred.
